$description: Trompe design tokens in W3C Design Tokens Community Group (DTCG) format. Every token becomes a CSS custom property named --tr-<path joined by dashes>, e.g. color.surface -> --tr-color-surface. Tokens with $extensions['dev.trompe'].dark have a dark-theme value; the generated CSS uses light-dark() so the active color-scheme picks the value.

surface.$description: Default color of a raised surface (panels, neutral buttons) before material is applied.

well.$description: Color of recessed areas: input wells, slider grooves, switch tracks.

ink-muted.$description: Secondary text, labels, placeholder-adjacent text. Meets 4.5:1 on surface.

edge.$description: Boundary of every interactive control. Meets 3:1 against canvas and surface so controls never rely on shadow alone.

accent.$description: Brand/action color (warm amber-orange by default, like an indicator lamp). Set --tr-color-accent to re-theme. Light value keeps accent-ink text at 4.5:1.

danger.$description: Destructive action and error text color. Meets 4.5:1 as text on canvas and surface.

success.$description: Positive status (completed, up, healthy). Meets 4.5:1 as text on canvas.

warning.$description: Caution status. A bright amber surface: pair with warning-ink, and use ink, not warning, for warning text on canvas.

shadow.$description: Base color of cast and ambient shadows. Alpha is applied by components from realism and depth.

highlight.$description: Base color of specular highlights and bevel light edges.

angle.$description: Direction the global light comes FROM, in CSS gradient convention: 0deg = top, 90deg = right, clockwise. All shadows and highlights agree on it. Registered with @property so it can be animated or overridden per subtree.

elevation.$description: Height of the light above the surface. Lower = longer shadows. 90deg = straight overhead (no offset).

environment.$description: Direction mirror finishes reflect from: 180deg puts the bright sky at the top and the dark horizon below the middle, like chrome outdoors. The light angle tilts it slightly.

realism.$description: The realism dial, 0..1. Scales shadows, gradients, grain and specular highlights. 0 = flat (edges only), 1 = full material realism. Set the realism attribute (flat|soft|tactile|real) on any element, or --tr-realism to any number.

flat.$description: No shadows or textures. Edges and colors only.

soft.$description: Subtle tactile depth. Good for productivity apps.

real.$description: Full material realism: grain, brushed metal, specular glints.

depth.$description: Depth is how far a surface sits above (positive) or below (negative) its parent, as an integer level -2..4 set with the depth attribute. The physical offset grows non-linearly: offset = pow(|level|, curve) * unit * light length, so every level reads as clearly higher than the last.

unit.$description: Physical offset of depth level 1 under a 45deg light.

curve.$description: Exponent applied to the level. 1 = linear; higher = upper levels separate more.

pill.$description: Fully rounded ends (switch tracks, pill buttons).

control.$description: Control heights per size, in em of the control's own font size, so a whole interface scales by changing font-size on a container (for example with container query units). On coarse pointers all sizes grow to at least the touch target.

touch.$description: Minimum hit area on coarse pointers.

family.$value: ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, "Segoe UI", Roboto, "Helvetica Neue", sans-serif

size.$description: Component font sizes relative to the inherited font size. Trompe scales with font-size like native controls.

release.$description: A control springing back (colour, opacity and short release transitions).

return.$description: A pressed cap returning on its spring, with a small overshoot. Baked from the 'press' spring; pair with --tr-motion-easing-return.

travel.$description: A thumb or cap travelling (switch throw).

throw.$description: A switch thumb or selector snapping over to its new position. Baked from the 'throw' spring; pair with --tr-motion-easing-throw.

settle.$description: A part dropping into a notch or snap point. Baked from the 'detent' spring; pair with --tr-motion-easing-settle.

glide.$description: A value travelling to a target set by code or keyboard, no overshoot. Baked from the 'glide' spring; pair with --tr-motion-easing-glide.

lift.$description: A menu, popover or dialog lifting off the page.

lamp.$description: An LED or indicator lamp lighting (off is twice as long, like a cooling filament).

press-min.$description: Shortest visible press. A quick tap is held down at least this long so it is always seen.

spring.$description: Slight overshoot, like a sprung mechanism. Uses the CSS linear() easing function.

return.$description: A pressed cap returning on its spring, with a small overshoot. Spring 'press' {"duration":0.22,"bounce":0.28} baked to CSS linear() by springEasing().

throw.$description: A switch thumb or selector snapping over to its new position. Spring 'throw' {"duration":0.16,"bounce":0.18} baked to CSS linear() by springEasing().

settle.$description: A part dropping into a notch or snap point. Spring 'detent' {"duration":0.12,"bounce":0.12} baked to CSS linear() by springEasing().

glide.$description: A value travelling to a target set by code or keyboard, no overshoot. Spring 'glide' {"duration":0.32,"bounce":0} baked to CSS linear() by springEasing().

material.$description: Materials are parameter bundles describing a substance. Components are geometry that only read these parameters, so any component can be any material. Apply with the material attribute (on a component) or data-tr-material (on any container). Each parameter is also a CSS variable, --tr-m-<param>, that you can set directly for custom materials.

plastic.$description: Smooth molded plastic with a soft satin sheen. The default.

ink.$description: Text and icon color on this material. Checked for contrast against base and both ends of its gradients.

specular.$description: Strength of highlights facing the light, 0..1.

roughness.$description: Spread of highlights. 0 = mirror-sharp, 1 = fully diffuse.

metalness.$description: 0..1. Metals tint their highlights with the base color and darken their shading.

spin.$description: Strength of concentric spun-metal reflections on round parts, 0..1.

gloss.$description: Clear-coat strength, 0..1: a crisp window reflection toward the light and a caustic glow opposite.

mirror.$description: Environment reflection, 0..1: chrome-like sky / horizon / ground bands that follow the light.

translucency.$description: How much of what is behind shows through, 0..1. Glass blurs it.

bevel.$description: Width of the light-catching rim at the edge.

finish.$description: Finishes override how a material reflects light without changing its color: set the finish attribute (component) or data-tr-finish (container). Each is a bundle of --tr-f-<param> variables that take precedence over the material's own values.

gloss.$description: Clear-coated: crisp window reflection and caustic glow, like lacquer or candy plastic.

mirror.$description: Polished mirror reflecting sky, horizon and ground.

spun.$description: Concentric spun reflections, for round caps and knobs.

profile.$description: Profiles describe the cross-section of a surface: how it curves under the light. Set the profile attribute (component) or data-tr-profile (container). Bundles of --tr-p-<param> variables.

flat.$description: Flat face with only a rim.

chamfer.$description: Width of the chamfered edge band.

convex.$description: Pillowed face that bulges toward the viewer.

chamfer.$description: Width of the chamfered edge band.

concave.$description: Dished face, like a fingertip dimple on a key or fader cap.

chamfer.$description: Width of the chamfered edge band.

dome.$description: Strongly spherical, for round buttons and knobs.

chamfer.$description: Width of the chamfered edge band.

bevel.$description: Flat face with a wide chamfered edge, like machined metal or a bezel.

chamfer.$description: Width of the chamfered edge band.
